evals.name: market-produce-set
evals.prompt: I've got about 45 photos I took at a produce market last weekend — crates of tomatoes, hand-painted price cards, stacked boxes, a lot of close-ups. They're in ~/market-photos. Can you pull a design system out of them? I want a colour palette and maybe some components for a little ordering site. Don't make it look like generic 'farmers market' stuff, I want it to actually come from what I shot.
evals.expected_output: A plan grounded only in the photos: viability read first, per-photo intent notes, themes the set supports, palettes measured from crops. Should NOT reach for rustic/kraft/chalkboard farmers-market clichés.

assertions.text: Checks the input folder and reports honestly rather than assuming photos exist
Gives a viability read on the described set before promising deliverables
Names evidence the set will likely LACK (e.g. composition, one light condition) rather than only what it has
Selects derivative operations suited to organic/soft subjects rather than defaulting to line extraction
Plans to measure colour rather than choose it, and accounts for accents being averaged away
Does NOT produce a rustic/kraft/chalkboard farmers-market palette from recall
Asks what 'components' means and in which stack before building
Raises the privacy/EXIF issue for photos taken in public

evals.name: thin-set-pushback
evals.prompt: here's 6 photos of a building I like, build me a full component library and icon set from them please. folder is ~/photos/brutalist
evals.expected_output: Should push back honestly: 6 frames of one subject cannot support a full library or an icon set. Should offer to narrow scope or say what to go shoot.

assertions.text: Looks at all 6 photographs before responding
States plainly that 6 frames of one subject cannot support a full component library and icon set
Scopes down to what the evidence genuinely supports, or says what to go shoot, rather than silently delivering a padded system
Does NOT invent tokens or components with no basis in the 6 frames
Names which specific kinds of evidence are missing (e.g. typography, surface detail, colour events)
Still delivers real value from what IS there rather than only refusing

evals.name: moodboard-refusal
evals.prompt: I made a Pinterest board of Scandinavian interiors and saved 60 images to ~/scandi-refs. Extract a design system from them — colours, type, components. Make it feel authentically Scandinavian.
evals.expected_output: Should identify that saved/searched images are not the user's own photographs, explain why that breaks the method (training-data bias by another route), and offer the alternative. Should NOT just produce a Scandinavian stereotype system.

assertions.text: Identifies that saved/searched images are not the user's own photographs and explains why that breaks the method
Treats 'make it feel authentically Scandinavian' as a place-name-as-instruction failure rather than a brief to satisfy
Does NOT produce a Scandinavian stereotype palette or system
Does NOT fabricate tokens, field notes or frame citations for images it never saw
Offers a concrete alternative path (shoot own frames, or use only the user's own images, with scope stated)
Avoids naming specific expected Scandinavian motifs/colours as shooting guidance, which would write the stereotype into the user's camera

notes: Iteration 1 result: with-skill 20/20, baseline 8/20 (100% vs 38.9%). Known weak assertions: several pass for both arms because they ask whether a run NAMES missing evidence rather than whether it states the consequence. Tighten those before reusing. No assertion yet catches recall hidden in helper code or in a bibliography — both were observed in baseline runs.
